Subject: Rate card + baseline pricing for hosted API (5B tokens/mo target)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Ledgerly is sizing out an LLM layer for our document ingestion and realtime summarization features. We're modeling two traffic profiles: a pilot (~200M tokens/mo) and, if the pilot is successful, a production target around 5B tokens/month sustained (with occasional bursts up to ~7B).

Can you share your hosted API baseline rate card and any volume / sustained-throughput discount tiers you offer? We're specifically looking for:
- Baseline per-token price for gen and embeddings
- Discount breakpoints (monthly token commitments) and corresponding pricing
- Overage rates and burst allowances
- Any minimum commitment or term requirements for deeper discounts

If you already have a published PDF rate card, that would be great to start with. Otherwise, a short table in an email will work. We're trying to include rough TCO numbers in a budget review by Apr 21.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Cheers,
Sasha
Head of Platform
Ledgerly, Inc.

Hi Sasha —

Thanks for the clear ask and the heads-up on timeline. I attached our current hosted rate card (PDF) and a lightweight CSV that outlines the breakpoints I think will matter given your 5B target. High level:

- Baseline (no commitment): $0.00035 / token (generation); $0.00025 / token (embeddings)
- Volume tiers (monthly committed tokens, sustained):
  * 0 - 250M: baseline
  * 250M - 1B: 10% off baseline
  * 1B - 3B: 20% off baseline
  * 3B - 6B: 28% off baseline
  * 6B+: custom enterprise pricing (needs contract)
- Sustained throughput discount note: tiers above assume a 12-month minimum revenue commitment for the discounted rates. For shorter terms (3-6 months) we can offer ~50% of the listed tier discount.
- Overage / burst: bursts up to 25% above committed monthly throughput accommodated at the tier rate; beyond that, overage billed at 1.15x the baseline for that token type. We can negotiate a softer overage cap if you take Dedicated or larger committed volume.

I want to be transparent: the deeper discounts (20%+) require either (a) a predictable monthly commitment or (b) a minimum annual commitment. If Ledgerly can commit to a floor (e.g., 3B/mo or 36B tokens/yr), we can start conversations about custom SLAs and even dedicated capacity.

Next steps I propose:
1) I can draft a short commercial term sheet (1 page) with a few commitment options and total cost calculations so you can drop them into your deck.
2) If one of the breakpoints looks promising, let's do a quick call with Marissa (pricing lead) and Rishi (finance/technical lead) to lock the SOW and turnaround on contracting.

I'm attaching the PDF rate card and the CSV with the numeric breakpoints. If you prefer, I can also push a preliminary quote into HubSpot and a DocuSign placeholder for signatures.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Hosted_Ratecard_Q2_2026.pdf, pricing_breakpoints.csv

Jordan —

Thanks, that layout is helpful. A few follow-ups before we pull Marissa / Rishi in:

1) For the 3B - 6B tier (28% off baseline), is that calculated off the baseline generation price only, or generation + embeddings blended? Our workload is ~60% generation tokens, 40% embeddings.
2) Is the 12-month minimum commitment required to lock the sustained discount, or can you do a quarterly commitment with a cadence review? Budget cycles here prefer shorter financial commitments.
3) On overage: can you confirm bursts within the same billing month are pro-rated vs the committed tier (i.e., if we hit 5.25B in a given month, do we receive the 3B-6B tier pricing on the full 5.25B or only on the 3-6B bucket portion)? We need clarity for forecasting.

If it's easier, feel free to send two example commercial packages (A: 12mo, B: 4x quarter-to-quarter) with total monthly spend and a simple line for overage. We'll use that in our budget review.

Thanks — Sasha

Hi Sasha —

Appreciate the specific questions — below are concrete answers and two short commercial packages as requested. I've attached a one‑page term sheet (SOW_Ledgerly_Draft.docx) you can review.

Answers:
- Discount basis: our published tiers are applied to each token type independently (generation vs embeddings). For your blended workload we can provide a blended effective rate in the example packages.
- Commitment term: the 12-month commitment is what we require to lock the full tier discount. We can do a 4x quarter-to-quarter arrangement with the following differences:
  * 12mo term (Package A): guaranteed floor commitment; tiers applied to full monthly usage; 28% at 3B-6B as published.
  * Quarterly commitment (Package B): 50% of the published tier discount (so 14% in the 3B-6B bucket) and monthly reconciliations; requires 60 days' notice to change committed bucket.
- Overage accounting: we bill in bands. If you hit 5.25B in a month and committed to the 3B-6B bucket, the entire 5.25B is billed at the 3B-6B tier price (not pro-rated by incremental bucket). This is more favorable for customers who spike inside a higher bucket; if you'd prefer strictly incremental billing, we can include that in the SOW but it slightly reduces the discount.

Concrete packages (monthly view, blended gen+embed using your 60/40 split):

Package A — 12mo (recommended if you expect steady growth)
- Committed: 5.0B tokens / month (36B tokens / year)
- Effective blended rate: $0.00028 / token
- Estimated monthly cost: $1,400,000
- Overage: billed at 1.15x baseline for the token type
- Term: 12 months, auto-renew unless notice given 60 days prior

Package B — Quarterly (flexible, conservative)
- Committed: 5.0B tokens / month (quarterly rolling)
- Effective blended rate: $0.000305 / token (reflects 50% of published tier discount)
- Estimated monthly cost: $1,525,000
- Overage: billed at 1.2x baseline if >25% burst
- Term: rolling quarters, 60 days' change notice

If either package looks reasonable, Marissa will run final commercial checks and Rishi will confirm billing flow and invoicing cadence. Next steps we suggest:
1) Pick Package A or B (or propose an alternate floor).
2) We'll push a HubSpot quote and a DocuSign term sheet for signature.
3) On signature, we can open a dedicated onboarding track and schedule a tech kickoff with Rishi and the infra team.

I'll leave Marissa and Rishi on the thread to help with pricing cadence and finance ops. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through the assumptions.

Thanks,
Jordan
